title: ばかり
summary: ばかり is a noun meaning "just that". Every use is a kind of exaggeration: just happened, nothing but, a great deal of, and the links ばかりか and ばかりに.

blocks.text: **ばかり** is in essence a **noun**, so it can take だ after it. Its core is "just this and nothing else", used the way English uses "nothing but": as a **hyperbole**. Seen that way, its uses stop looking like a list.

After a **past** verb it says that nothing has happened since: the action is very recent. The past tense is needed because the idea is about something completed. This is an exaggeration too: you have had a walk and a talk since lunch, but "nothing else has happened".

blocks.jp: 昼ご飯を食べたばかりだ。
日本に来たばかりです。
blocks.en: I have just come to Japan.

blocks.text: 2. A great deal of one thing
After a noun it exaggerates: there is so much of it that it feels like nothing else exists.

blocks.jp: この町は観光客ばかりだ。
blocks.en: This town is nothing but tourists.

blocks.text: After a verb in the **て-form**, plus いる: you keep doing that and nothing else.

blocks.jp: 弟はゲームをしてばかりいる。
blocks.en: My little brother does nothing but play games.

blocks.text: **ばかりか** adds か, a question used to deny: "do you think that is all?" So ばかり is "only that", and ばかりか is "not only that". **ばかりに** adds に and means **"just because"**, with a stronger and usually unlucky cause than から or ので.

blocks.jp: 彼女は歌ったばかりか、踊った。
blocks.en: She did not only sing, she danced too.

blocks.jp: 傘を忘れたばかりに、濡れてしまった。
blocks.en: Just because I forgot my umbrella, I got wet.

blocks.jp: 耳が大きいばかりに、誰も遊んでくれない。
blocks.en: Just because my ears are big, nobody plays with me.

blocks.text: The uses of ばかり differ in what comes before it, so here they are next to each other.

items: **Past verb + ばかり**: just did it.
**Noun + ばかり**: nothing but / loads of.
**Verb て-form + ばかり + いる**: keeps doing only that.
**ばかりか**: not only, but also; **ばかりに**: just because.

questions.note: Past verb + ばかり: it just happened.

questions.prompt: この本は買った＿＿だ。でも、もうなくした。
questions.note: Past verb + ばかり: just did.
questions.en: I have just bought this book. But I already lost it.

options: 着いているばかりです
questions.note: The past form is needed: 着いた + ばかり.
Noun + ばかり: nothing but, so many that nothing else seems to exist.
questions.en: This shop is nothing but women.

questions.prompt: 彼は食べてばかりいる。
options: He eats a great deal of rice
questions.note: て-form + ばかり + いる: keeps doing only that.
て-form + ばかりいる.
questions.en: My little sister does nothing but sleep.

questions.prompt: 彼は英語＿＿、中国語も話せる。
questions.note: ばかりか: not only that, but also.
questions.en: He speaks not only English but also Chinese.

questions.prompt: かぎを忘れた＿＿、家に入れなかった。
questions.note: ばかりに: just because (an unlucky cause).
questions.en: Just because I forgot the key, I could not get in.
